body:
Chief: I APPLIED THE CORRECTED RANKING PRINCIPLE TO THE SLICES I HAD ALREADY SCOPED, AND IT MOVED TWO MORE TYPES TO THE FRONT. This is the follow-through on the AuthorizedRemoteRequest correction, and the pattern is now unmistakable: every time I rank by what a type PROMISES instead of by whether it validates ITSELF, something important comes up from the bottom.

CREDENCE - core, slice 2, promoted to FIRST in that slice. Its Scaladoc: "Invariant: a calibrated value is present only if the calibration model that produced it is named." That is not merely a comment. IT IS DESIGN-CONTRACT RULE 3 - Credence.rawScore is never a probability unless a calibrationModel is recorded - one of the thirteen non-negotiables at the top of AGENTS.md. Credence is a case class with a private constructor, so fromProduct mints a CALIBRATED PROBABILITY WITH NO NAMED MODEL in one line. Nine modules carry it: amr-interop, codec, core, features, fixtures, interview, laws, proposition, story. A calibrated probability whose provenance is unnamed is precisely the thing that must never reach a paper, and our own rulebook forbids it while the type permits it.

COVERAGE - features, slice 3, promoted. Its Scaladoc: "every aggregate must say how much of its support it actually observed", and construction is validated so observed is at most eligible and both are nonnegative. EIGHT MODULES carry it: acquire, align, codec, embed-bench, embed-core, features, interview, laws. Coverage is THE SUPPORT CARRIER that ADR 0003 leans on - the entire "support travels with the estimate" edifice assumes a Coverage means what it says. Forge one and you get observed exceeding eligible, or negative counts, and a fraction above one; attach it to an estimate and the support claim is simply false. Note also that Coverage.+ constructs directly without revalidating - safe for two valid operands, but it means a forged Coverage PROPAGATES through every aggregate it touches.

THE PATTERN, stated because it should change how everyone reads this sweep: THE WORST TYPES TO LEAVE FORGEABLE ARE THE ONES WHOSE DOCUMENTATION MAKES A PROMISE. AuthorizedRemoteRequest promises no code path can hand raw text to a provider. CheckedSidecarPrelude promises verification against evidence outside the file. Credence promises a calibrated value implies a named model. Coverage promises an aggregate says how much support it observed. Four types, four promises, all currently false, and NOT ONE of them was ranked highly by my original self-validation heuristic - three had no self-validating companion at all.

FEATURES/estimate.scala IS RESERVED to the scout right now for MissingReason.Custom, so Coverage cannot be touched today and I am not asking anyone to. This is ranking, not scheduling.

I have written both promotions onto the sweep bead. If anyone picking up a slice finds a type whose Scaladoc makes a promise I have not ranked accordingly, move it up and tell me - my ordering has now been wrong three times in the same direction, and the direction is always that I under-rank the types that promise the most.
